items.s: After running a marathon, he was completely ____ and went straight to bed.

items.s: In August 2026, scientists ____ a study about weekend sleep.
But then you remember something you have ____ many times.
The adults in the survey ____ more at weekends than on weekdays.
Not ____ enough sleep may put extra pressure on the body.
High blood pressure ____ the risk of heart disease and stroke.

tfn.s: Most South Korean adults sleep later at weekends than on weekdays.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say how many South Korean adults sleep later at weekends.

tfn.s: The researchers used information from around 40,000 adults in South Korea.
tfn.why: The text says: "They looked at information from around 40,000 adults in South Korea over seven years."

tfn.s: People who slept much longer than usual did not get the same benefits.
tfn.why: The text says: "People who slept much longer than usual did not appear to get the same benefits."

tfn.s: The research proved that a weekend lie-in prevents high blood pressure.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "The research found a connection, but it did not prove that a weekend lie-in directly prevents high blood pressure."

tfn.s: The study says that everyone should sleep until lunchtime on Sunday.
tfn.why: The text says: "the study does not mean that everyone should sleep until lunchtime on Sunday."

get better, or get your energy back
good things that you get from something
the things you do in the same way every day
a link between two things
make something go wrong
the chance that something bad will happen
change something, or have an effect on it

focus.note: Think about the idea each word brings: a reason, a result, a contrast, a condition or a choice.

items.s: The doctor says sleep is important ____ it helps the body recover.
It was Saturday, ____ Maria stayed in bed for an extra hour.
____ the alarm was off, Tom woke up at seven.
____ you want a calm Sunday, try switching off your phone.
Go to bed earlier tonight, ____ you will feel tired tomorrow.
The company made only a ____ profit this year, far less than expected.
Many students ____ to find quiet places to study in noisy cities.
Carrying heavy bags every day can put a ____ on your back.
Rain is not a good ____ for missing the meeting.
Please do not ____ him while he is working, because he needs to concentrate.
A year abroad is a great ____ to practise a language.

match.d: continuing although you have no energy left
reduce the amount of something you use or do
take care of somebody or something
staying much the same from one day to the next

items.s: The bridge ____ in 1998 and still carries traffic today.
When she got to the station, the train ____ already.
I ____ to bed earlier; now I feel terrible.
She suggested ____ a short walk after lunch.
If I ____ more time, I would learn the piano.

tfn.s: The study proved that staying in bed directly lowers blood pressure.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "The study showed an association, not proof that staying in bed directly reduces the risk of hypertension."

tfn.s: The research was discussed at a European heart conference in August 2026.
tfn.why: The text says: "However, research discussed at a European heart conference in August 2026 suggests that a modest amount of catch-up sleep may be helpful."

tfn.s: Researchers warned that very long weekend lie-ins could disturb sleep patterns.
tfn.why: The text says: "Researchers also warned that very long weekend lie-ins could disturb regular sleep patterns."

tfn.s: The study found that women benefited more than men.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not compare the results for women and men.

tfn.s: The most favourable amount of extra sleep was less than ninety minutes.
tfn.why: An extra hour and twenty-seven minutes is eighty-seven minutes, which is less than ninety.

the bad feeling when you think you did something wrong
a connection between two things

easy to understand, with nothing difficult in it

focus.note: Decide if the idea is contrast, reason or result. Some of these words join two sentences and some need a noun.

items.s: The new phone is expensive. ____, many people think it is worth the money.
My sister enjoys early mornings, ____ I prefer to sleep late.
____ the long hours, she still finds time to exercise.
Take a break now; ____, you will be too tired to finish the work.
The roads were closed; ____, the buses were late.
The headline was blunt, but the full report contained far more ____ than the press coverage suggested.
The charity launched an urgent appeal to cover a ____ of nearly half its budget.
Strikes on the railways are likely to ____ travel plans across the region.
No amount of money can fully ____ for the loss of a family home.
The firm reported a ____ increase in profits, far beyond what analysts had predicted.
The hotel was merely ____: clean and quiet enough, but nothing special.

match.d: remove the effect of something else
allowing yourself more pleasure than you should
manage several demands at the same time

items.s: The scientists were careful to avoid any ____ when describing the results.
The ____ of the findings is limited because other factors were not checked.
It would be ____ to assume that one study settles the question.
The ____ between sleep and mood is hard to measure precisely.
He is a highly ____ athlete who trains every morning.

tfn.s: The conclusions rest on observing people's habits rather than controlling them.
tfn.why: The researchers "did not assign people different amounts of weekend sleep", so they observed existing habits.

tfn.s: The text suggests that sleeping until midday may bring the same benefits as an extra hour.
tfn.why: Very large differences in routine can disrupt the body clock, so midday is called "a very different proposition".

tfn.s: The study found that desk workers benefited more than manual workers.
tfn.why: Occupation is mentioned only as a possible influence; no groups are compared.

tfn.s: The writer implies that early risers are not necessarily less tired than late risers.
tfn.why: Neither being called lazy nor being praised for discipline "tells us much about how tired those people actually are".

tfn.s: The writer treats the figure of one hour and twenty-seven minutes as an exact instruction for everyone.
tfn.why: The text says it would be misleading to interpret it "as an exact prescription for every tired adult".

the fact that one thing makes another happen

focus.note: Some of these words take a noun, some a clause, and some mark a concession or a result. Check the punctuation before the gap.

speak.title: Role-play: a quiet Saturday morning
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.role: the flatmate who wants to sleep late
a.text: It's Saturday and you've had a long, tiring week. You want to stay in bed until ten. Explain why, and suggest a plan that works for both of you.

b.role: the flatmate who wants an early start
b.text: You want to go out for breakfast at eight and then tidy the flat. Ask your flatmate to join you. Listen to their reasons and try to agree on a compromise.

phrases: I'd really like to stay in bed this morning.
It's been a long week and I'm exhausted.
Could we go for breakfast a bit later?
I'd rather start early, if that's okay.
That's fair, so how about we meet at nine?
Let's compromise: you tidy now and I'll cook later.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: what did you agree, and was it a fair compromise?
